places.name: Markt
places.note: Market square with the City Hall on one side 'across from the Nieuwe Kerk'.

places.name: Nieuwe Kerk
places.note: Vermeer was baptised here; holds the tomb of William of Orange; its sunlit tower is the focus of View of Delft. The present stone spire dates from 1875.

places.name: Stadhuis (City Hall)
places.note: Renaissance building designed by Hendrick de Keyser on the Markt opposite the Nieuwe Kerk; the tower 'De Steen' dates from around 1300.

places.name: Oude Kerk
places.coord_source: OSM way 239895200 (bbox centre), addr Heilige Geestkerkhof 25
places.note: Vermeer was buried here on 15 December 1675 (VERIFIED: en and nl Wikipedia). 75 m brick tower leaning about two metres. Two grave markers: one of 1975, a larger one of 2007.

places.name: Site of Vermeer's home, Oude Langendijk at the corner of the Molenpoort (now Jozefstraat)
places.coord_source: OSM: junction node of ways 311563376 (Oude Langendijk) and 7538976 ('Jozefstraat voorheen Molenpoort')
places.note: The house of his mother-in-law Maria Thins, next to a hidden Jesuit church; the house is gone. WHICH CORNER IS DISPUTED: the traditional site is the east corner (house 'Serpent'), now covered by the neo-Gothic Maria van Jessekerk (built 1875-1882); research by H.G. Slager (2017, 2018, 2024) puts it on the west corner (house 'Trapmolen', today's Oude Langendijk 25). A commemorative plaque is at the corner.

places.name: Maria van Jessekerk
places.note: Neo-Gothic Catholic church of 1875-1882 on the ground of the 17th-century Jesuit hidden church; did not exist in Vermeer's day.

places.name: Site of the Mechelen inn, Markt at the corner of the Oude Manhuissteeg
places.coord_source: OSM: junction node of Markt (way 125227122) and Oude Manhuissteeg (way 125227133)
places.note: Inn bought by Vermeer's father in 1641, where Vermeer grew up (he was not born there). Markt 54-56, demolished in 1885; no building stands in its place. The alley behind it leads to a bridge over the Voldersgracht. A 1955 tablet on the adjoining Markt 52 marks the spot and wrongly says he was born there.

places.name: St Luke's Guild site, now Vermeer Centrum Delft, Voldersgracht 21
places.exists_today_note: The present building is a reconstruction; the 17th-century guild house does not survive.
places.note: Historic location of the Guild of St Luke (former chapel of the Oude Manhuis, converted to a guild house from 1661); Vermeer joined the guild on 29 December 1653 and was headman in 1662, 1663, 1670 and 1671. Original pulled down in the 19th century: sources disagree on the year (1876 or 1879 on Essential Vermeer pages; 1886 on nl Wikipedia). A school stood there, then the reconstruction; the Vermeer Centrum opened in 2007.

places.name: Voldersgracht (canal)
places.note: Vermeer's parents kept the inn De Vliegende Vos in the family home on the Voldersgracht.

places.name: Oude Delft (canal)
places.note: Main north-south canal of the old town; the Kapelsbrug crossed it between the two south gates.

places.name: Kolk (Zuidkolk) harbour
places.coord_source: OSM way 270579738 (natural=water, name Zuidkolk, bbox centre)
places.note: Triangular harbour at the south edge of town, dug 1614-1620; the water in the foreground of View of Delft. It keeps its original shape and scale.

places.name: Viewpoint of View of Delft, Hooikade (south bank of the Kolk)
places.coord_source: OSM way 39941510 (Hooikade, bbox centre). nl Wikipedia gives the painting's coordinates as 52.00417, 4.36111.
places.exists_today_note: The quay exists; the house Vermeer looked out from does not.
places.note: Vermeer painted from an upper floor of a house on the Schie looking across the Kolk (nl Wikipedia: 'een bovenhuis aan de Schie'; Essential Vermeer: second storey of an inn long since demolished). OSM shows Hooikade as the street along the south bank of the Zuidkolk. No fetched text source names Hooikade as the viewpoint: the street name is UNVERIFIED as a sourced statement, verified only by map position.

places.name: Schiedam Gate (Schiedamse Poort), former position
places.coord_source: nl Wikipedia article coordinates (approximate, rounded to arc-seconds)
places.note: City gate in the middle of View of Delft, with a clock and bell on it; stood beside the Rotterdam Gate, joined to it by the Kapelsbrug over the Oude Delft. Demolished: 1836 per nl Wikipedia, 1834 per Essential Vermeer. Nothing remains.

places.name: Rotterdam Gate (Rotterdamse Poort), former position
places.coord_source: nl Wikipedia article coordinates (approximate, rounded to arc-seconds)
places.note: Twin-turreted gate at the right of View of Delft, near the Armamentarium where the Schie meets the town canals. Demolished 1834-1836 (nl Wikipedia; Essential Vermeer says 1836). Nothing remains.

places.name: Armamentarium (arsenal)
places.note: The long red-roofed arsenal behind the Schiedam Gate in View of Delft; the building is mapped in OSM today.

places.name: Proposed location of The Little Street, Vlamingstraat 40-42
places.coord_source: OSM node 3844955479 ('Straatje van Vermeer', wikidata Q586035)
places.exists_today_note: The plots exist; the houses in the painting do not.
places.note: A PROPOSAL, not a settled fact: art historian Frans Grijzenhout argued in 2015, from the Delft quay-dues register, that the painting shows the plots now numbered Vlamingstraat 40 and 42; the house on the right belonged to Vermeer's aunt Ariaentgen Claes van der Minne, who sold tripe. Earlier candidates were the Voldersgracht and Nieuwe Langendijk 22-26 (demolished 1982).

places.name: Oostpoort (East Gate)
places.note: The only one of Delft's original eight city gates still standing; raised in 1519. Useful as a model for the two lost gates.
